## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e98c3c93c95beb28885b944b289c46bfe4021e94`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card objectui#11011 (body; triage 5874675337; claim 5923408921; `os-dev-report` 5923854743), PR #11316 (body, 2-file list, the API diff — byte-identical, index lines aside, to `git diff` from the merge-base `caa0cd3` to the head), the head's check-runs (read three times, 03:05Z to 03:14Z), the repository at `main` (`cd5b19a`, the PR's base sha) and at the head, PR objectui#11010's merge commit `ad0310fb5` through the API. Nothing built, run or re-run. ⛔ Not the dispatch order, not the dispatching seat's conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The new fence — true at the head, and not copyable into a crash.** `AppShell`, `AdapterProvider` and `MetadataProvider` are exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` (its "Components" and "Providers" export lines). `AppShellProps` in app-shell's `types.ts` declares `sidebar?: ReactNode` and `children: ReactNode`; the component renders `children` inside its `main` element, so `AppShell` takes children. `AdapterProviderProps` declares `adapter?: ObjectStackAdapter | null`; `MetadataProviderProps` declares `adapter: ObjectStackAdapter` — the fence's `adapter={myAdapter}` on both, and `sidebar={‹MySidebar /›}`, name props that exist. The fence is a fragment (`myAdapter` and `MySidebar` are undeclared) carrying no `os:check` marker, so no gate compiles it and nothing claims it compiles; with the identifiers supplied it renders two providers and an empty main — no `objects.find` is reachable, so no first-render throw. One observation, not a defect: TypeScript counts a comment-only child as no child, so a copy that leaves the slot holding only the JSX comment is refused at compile time for the missing required `children` — a refusal, not a crash, on a placeholder whose own text ("your React Router routes — ObjectView mounts on an object route, see below") tells the reader to replace it.

**(b) Every added prose sentence, read at the code.**
- "`react-router-dom` is its peer dependency" — TRUE: `packages/app-shell/package.json` `peerDependencies` carries `"react-router-dom": "^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0"`, unchanged across `b28bde8`, `caa0cd3` and `cd5b19a`.
- "`ObjectView` resolves the object and view from the route" — TRUE: in `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`, `ObjectView` reads `const { objectName } = useParams();` and `ObjectViewInner` reads `const { appName, objectName, viewId } = useParams();`, both from `react-router-dom`; the resolution is an `objects.find` matching `o.name === objectName`, unguarded, in the outer wrapper — so the removed mount (no `objects`) still throws on first render on today's code, as the card's class (a) said, and now also fails to compile.
- "the console mounts it on `/apps/:appName/:objectName` and `/apps/:appName/:objectName/view/:viewId`" — TRUE: `apps/console/src/App.tsx` declares `Route path="/apps/:appName/*"` rendering the console's `AppContent`, a "thin wrapper around DefaultAppContent" that renders app-shell's `DefaultAppContent` with `extraRoutes={systemRoutes}`; that component's `Routes` declares `Route path=":objectName"` and `Route path=":objectName/view/:viewId"`, each rendering `ObjectView dataSource={dataSource} objects={allObjects} onEdit={handleEdit} externalRefreshKey={refreshKey}`. The README's own "### ObjectView" prose names the same two paths.
- "so it takes no `objectName` prop" and "Its props are the exported `ConsoleObjectViewProps` — `dataSource`, `objects`, `onEdit`, and the optional `externalRefreshKey`" — TRUE: the interface declares exactly `dataSource: DataSource`, `objects: any[]`, `onEdit` (a function taking the record to edit, returning void), `externalRefreshKey?: number`, no `objectName`; it is re-exported as a type from `views/index.ts` and the package entry, both brought by `ad0310fb5` (PR objectui#11010, merged 2026-09-28T17:09Z).
- "Copy the mount from the "ObjectView" section of `packages/app-shell/README.md`: that block is the one `pnpm check:doc-snippets` compiles" — TRUE, see (c). "The one" holds: the only other `ObjectView` mounts in gated documents (root `README.md`, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`, `packages/plugin-view/README.md`) and in `examples/byo-backend-console/README.md` mount `@object-ui/plugin-view`'s schema-driven `ObjectView`, a different component, and `examples/**` is outside the gate's roots anyway.

**(c) The pointer lands on a gated copy.** `packages/app-shell/README.md` has the `### ObjectView` heading at the head (between `### AppShell` and `### DashboardView / PageView`); its `tsx` block imports `ObjectView, type ConsoleObjectViewProps` and mounts `dataSource`, `objects`, `onEdit`, `externalRefreshKey={0}` — the hunk `ad0310fb5` added. `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` (`pnpm check:doc-snippets`) collects, in `listDocuments`, `content/docs`, every `apps/‹app›/docs`, every `packages/‹pkg›/README.md`, nested package READMEs, top-level `docs/`, `docs/adr`, `docs/audits` and the root `README.md`; its rule is opt-out — "EVERY `ts` / `tsx` fenced block in a covered document is compiled, in ISOLATION, as its own module. A block that is not meant to compile must be DECLARED by a marker line immediately above its fence" (the `doc-snippet: fragment` HTML comment in `FRAGMENT_MARKER_EXAMPLES`). No such marker sits above the README block, so it is compiled; the head's "Doc Snippet Type Check" is `success` (4m40s: build, then compile). The same header states "⛔ `skills/objectui/**` is NOT claimed by any gate here", which is exactly why pointing beats restating. The dev's premise 3 reads right.

**(d) No new gate.** Two files, neither under `scripts/` nor `.github/`; nothing extends any root. Triage's 「新增门禁默认否」 is honoured.

**(e) `os:check` markers.** The guide's five markers sit above `json` fences and are untouched (identical positions at `main` and head; the edit starts after them). The edited `tsx` fence was unmarked at `main` and stays unmarked — correctly, since it is a fragment `check-skill-examples.mjs` could not compile ("a self-contained, should-hold-up block is opted in"). "Skill Example Check" `success` on the head ("Every marked skill example holds up", per the dev; the check-run is the verdict).

**(f) AGENTS.md rule #11.** A regex scan of the PR body, the changeset and every added line for `path:line` and `#L` forms finds none; paths are cited bare (`packages/app-shell/README.md`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`, `packages/app-shell/src/console/AppContent.tsx`) and symbols by name. "Line Citation Gate" `success`.

**(g) The +6 net lines, judged by their reader.** The guide goes 345 to 351 lines, 1234 to 1301 words. Rule lines an agent setting up a project needs: runs under React Router with `react-router-dom` as peer dependency; no `objectName` prop; the four `ConsoleObjectViewProps` members; the pointer to the README block. Commentary a reader pays for on every read: the parenthetical naming the console's two route paths (the README the reader is sent to states them), and the tail clause "that block is the one `pnpm check:doc-snippets` compiles, and this guide does not restate it" (gate provenance a project-setup reader does not act on). The paragraph could be about four lines without losing a true rule. Advisory: no ceiling exists (no skills size ratchet in objectui; `check-skill-eval-tokens` is a token oracle, see ③), triage asked for precisely "point" plus "say that it runs under a router", and every sentence is true. One more advisory note: the pointer is a repo path; the README ships in the tarball (`files` lists `README.md`), so an npm consumer reads it at `node_modules/@object-ui/app-shell/README.md`, and inline-span repo paths are the guide's convention (`check-skills-paths` resolves them against the tree; "Skill Guide Path Check" `success`).

**(h) The replaced sentence.** At `main` the guide read "App-shell is router-agnostic — wire it into React Router / Next.js / TanStack Router yourself." False there: the same peer dependency and the same `useParams`, `useSearchParams`, `useNavigate`, `useLocation` imports in `ObjectView.tsx` predate `ad0310fb5` (unchanged context in that diff), and `useNavigate` throws outside a React Router context, so a Next.js or TanStack host could not mount `ObjectView`. Gone at the head: `git grep` for "router-agnostic" over `skills/`, app-shell's README and its manifest finds nothing. Nuance, not a defect: the `AppShell` layout component itself is router-free (its docblock: "Provides basic application structure without routing or console-specific logic"); the new sentence is about the package and `ObjectView`, which is what the paragraph teaches.

**`main` movement.** Merge-base `caa0cd3`; `main` at review `cd5b19a`, five commits past the cut, PR `mergeable_state: behind`. The guide, app-shell's README, manifest, `index.ts`, `ObjectView.tsx`, console `AppContent.tsx` and both check scripts are byte-identical across `b28bde8`, `caa0cd3` and `cd5b19a`.

### ② Semver level

Nothing published changes. No package manifest's `files` names `skills/**` (grep over every workspace `package.json`: none); `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `files` is `dist`, `src/styles.css`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE`, none touched. `.changeset/11011-project-setup-objectview-mount.md` has an empty frontmatter (`---` then `---`) and a body; `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s header says "An EMPTY frontmatter counts", subtracts `*.md` as documentation, and nothing was owed (no guarded `src/**` in the diff). The empty-frontmatter changeset IS objectui's declared form for "publishes nothing": the repo's own pin in `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` ("never wires the phantom `skip-changeset` label into a workflow or a gate") says "To declare that a PR publishes nothing, add a changeset with empty frontmatter; that is the mechanism", and 46 such changesets sit in `.changeset/` at the head as precedent. Correction to the brief's premise: the labels API lists a `skip-changeset` label object on objectui at read time — the re-minted phantom that pin predicts ("one API call that applies the name mints the label again"); no workflow or script reads it, so its existence changes nothing. `Clause-②: no` is right: no accept set, no public surface, no shipped byte moves. "Changeset Declaration", "Changeset Bump Policy", "Changeset Overwrite Report", "Changeset Fixed Group Check": all `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`check:skill-eval-tokens` is not a size meter** — confirmed: `scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs`'s header reads "Every `must_contain` token of every `skills/‹bundle›/evals/*.json` must be something the skill bundle actually TEACHES", a bundle-wide oracle with no ceiling. The dispatch's "line budget" has no instrument in objectui; the dev's `wc` readings (+6 lines, +67 words, +520 bytes, labelled whitespace words) are the honest substitute. "Skill Eval Token Check" `success`. Answered.
- **`pnpm lint` as a proven narrowing** — valid: `eslint.config.js`'s `files` globs are all of the `**/*.{ts,tsx}` family or specific `.ts` paths, with no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project`, so linting is per-file and non-type-aware; a `.md` plus `.changeset/*.md` diff matches no config and moves no untouched file's verdict. CI's "Lint" `success` (15s) is `lint.yml`'s own "Only ignored paths changed. Skipping the steps below; this check still reports." path — a skip by design, recorded as such; the same holds for ci.yml's "Type Check".
- **`check-doc-snippet-types`, `check-readme-exports`, `spec-main-shape-gate` NOT MEASURED locally** — CI owns them and answered: "Doc Snippet Type Check" `success`, "README Export Check" `success`, "Spec Main Shape Gate" `success` (still `in_progress` at my 03:05Z read, completed by 03:13Z).
- **`origin/main` moved `b28bde8` to `caa0cd3` at cut** — judged in ①: nothing in the touched section, nor in any file the prose is about, moved in that interval or since.
- **`mcp_calls: 0` / `api_writes: 2`** — consistent with both threads: the PR by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, draft, 0 comments, 0 reviews, 0 issue events, no labels, no assignee, no auto-merge, no reviewers; the card carries the dev's one `os-dev-report`, and its `pm:dispatched`, `pm:queue` removal and `os-warren` assignment at 02:18–02:19Z are the PM's dispatch acts, not the dev's. Labels on the PR: none, and none were due — `.github/labeler.yml`'s `documentation` rule matches root `*.md` and `packages/**/README.md` only, so a `skills/**` plus `.changeset/**` diff draws nothing ("label" `success`). The dev declared "No label and no PR assignee written (seat does both)"; objectstack's claim paragraph expects the PR's assignee to mirror the card's at `pr_create`, so mirroring `os-warren` onto the PR is the seat's act on adoption — declared, not hidden.
- `open_questions: []`; two `out_of_scope_findings` noted and not filed (an advisory JSON-schema sweep line on `main`, and the dispatch's own wording) — both carriers "none", correctly.
- **Tier.** `skills/**` is `GOVERNED_SURFACES`'s `skills-catalog` row — Tier H: the PR stays draft until a latest-decisive APPROVED review by `os-zhuang` or `hotlong`, then the owning seat lands it. "Governed Surface Queue Guard" `success` on the `pull_request` leg is the early-warning leg exiting 0 by design, not a clearance.

**Check-runs on the head, final read 2026-10-01T03:14:39Z:** 41 check-runs — 38 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)`, `dependabot`), 0 `in_progress`, 0 `failure`. At my first read (03:05Z) 9 were `in_progress` (`Spec Main Shape Gate` and the eight `Test (shard N/8)`); all reached `success`, and the ci.yml fan-in `Test` (`needs: [test, test-dist-pins]`) completed `success` at 03:13:32Z. Required contexts per the ruleset API (`GET /rules/branches/main`, 8 contexts): `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Test`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — all eight `success`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-11011-project-setup-objectview-mount`
Reviewed-by: `session_01KTZmMfzVzjNvyaLyQ8mHvg`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

**改了什么**:发布给用户的 objectui 技能里,「项目起步」指南的 `@object-ui/app-shell` 一节原来教 `<ObjectView objectName="contact" />`——这个组件根本没有 `objectName` 这个 prop,照抄会在首次渲染时崩,PR #11010 之后更是直接编译报错。现在改为:示例只保留 Provider + AppShell 的骨架,正文指向 app-shell README 里被 `check:doc-snippets` 编译把关的那一份挂载代码,并如实说明它跑在 React Router 之下(`react-router-dom` 是 peer 依赖、从路由解析 objectName)、四个 prop 是什么。

**为什么改**:这是 AI 照抄的第一份文档,一句错话等于产品缺陷(北极星第 4 条)。分诊方向「指向而不复述,保持唯一一份在门禁之下」,本 PR 照此做,未新增门禁。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**:只改一节散文 + 一条空 changeset,不发包;不碰代码。复审(契约复审档,记录 5924031392)逐句对照源码核过。回滚 = revert。两处可再精简的修饰语(路由路径括号、门禁出处尾句)留给下次动这一节的 PR。

**席位意见**:建议批准。

**你要做的**:在本 PR 上留一条 APPROVED review(os-zhuang 或 hotlong);之后由本席翻 ready、挂 auto-merge 入队。
